**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

This rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position — the agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on IBM at all, rather than merely a narrowed one.

The key directional point is that every restriction-flavoured provision in this document binds MSL, not us. The planner's specific concern about § 14.18 is unfounded: despite its "Restrictions and Limitations" heading, it constrains MSL's use of IBM property and MSL's ability to perform competing Integration work — it places no limit on IBM's ability to build in-house or buy from other suppliers. Likewise § 16.15 restricts MSL's sourcing, which is a benefit to us.

I also confirmed the absence of the subtler form this rule can take: there is no requirements contract, minimum-purchase commitment, or sole-source obligation in the scope-of-work sections that would functionally lock IBM into MSL. And the confidentiality carve-out at p1490–1491 affirmatively protects our right to supply competitive products and to work with MSL's competitors.

One item I deliberately noted rather than flagged: § 9.0(f) does restrict IBM, via a time-limited non-solicit of Transferred Employees. I left it unflagged here because it restricts our hiring, not the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build, so it sits outside this rule's scope — and flagging it here would risk double-counting a term properly assessed under a non-solicitation rule. It is worth confirming that a NONSOLICIT rule exists in the playbook to pick it up, since the redacted duration ("[*] years") is the one term there that would merit a length check.
